evidence.intree_statement: Class Monoid (X : C) : Type := { mu : X ⨂ X ~> X; eta : I ~> X; mu_assoc : mu ∘ bimap mu id[X] ≈ mu ∘ bimap id[X] mu ∘ to tensor_assoc; mu_unit_left : mu ∘ bimap eta id[X] ≈ to (@unit_left C M X); mu_unit_right : mu ∘ bimap id[X] eta ≈ to (@unit_right C M X) }   (Context {C : Category}, `{M : @Monoidal C})

Class CommutativeMonoid (X : C) : Type := { cmon_monoid : @Monoid C (@braided_is_monoidal C (@symmetric_is_braided C S)) X; mu_commutative_of_cmon : (@mu _ _ _ cmon_monoid) ∘ braid ≈ (@mu _ _ _ cmon_monoid) }   (Context `{S : @SymmetricMonoidal C})

Class MonoidObject (mon : C) := { mempty : I ~> mon; mappend : mon ⨂ mon ~> mon; mempty_left : mappend ∘ bimap mempty id ≈ to (@unit_left C _ mon); mempty_right : mappend ∘ bimap id mempty ≈ to (@unit_right C _ mon); mappend_assoc : mappend ∘ bimap mappend id ≈ mappend ∘ bimap id mappend ∘ to tensor_assoc }

statement_record.book: A monoid object in a symmetric monoidal category (C, I, ⊗) is a triple (M, μ : M⊗M → M, η : I → M) satisfying (a) associativity (μ⊗id);μ = (id⊗μ);μ and (b) two-sided unitality (η⊗id);μ = id = (id⊗η);μ; it is a COMMUTATIVE monoid object when additionally (c) σ_{M,M};μ = μ for the symmetry σ. Coherence isomorphisms are suppressed because the ambient setting there is strict.
statement_record.intree: Class Monoid (X : C) with mu/eta and mu_assoc / mu_unit_left / mu_unit_right over an arbitrary `{M : @Monoidal C}; Class CommutativeMonoid (X : C) over `{S : @SymmetricMonoidal C} adding mu_commutative_of_cmon : mu ∘ braid ≈ mu. Structure/Monoid.v:124 gives the same class again under the names mempty/mappend.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger: the in-tree laws are stated over an ARBITRARY (non-strict) monoidal category with the associator `to tensor_assoc` and the unitors `to unit_left` / `to unit_right` written in explicitly, so the book's strict-setting suppression of coherence is the special case; clause (c) is stated with `braid` in a SymmetricMonoidal ambient, matching σ exactly. Equations are hom-setoid ≈ rather than =, the library's faithful rephrasing. Note the library carries TWO equivalent spellings of the same class (Theory/Algebra/Monoid.v's mu/eta and Structure/Monoid.v's mempty/mappend), and the dual (Comonoid, CommutativeComonoid) as well.

evidence.intree_statement: Definition Monoid_of_StrictPremonoidal {c : Category} (p : StrictPremonoidal c) : @MonoidObject StrictCat Funny_Monoidal c := @Build_MonoidObject StrictCat Funny_Monoidal c (sp_unit p) (sp_tensor p) (sp_unit_left p) (sp_unit_right p) (sp_assoc p)   — with the converse StrictPremonoidal_of_Monoid (:136) and both record-level round trips by reflexivity (roundtrip_monoid :165, roundtrip_strict_premonoidal :169). This is the SAME-SHAPED correspondence the example asserts, but taken at the FUNNY tensor □ rather than the cartesian product, so it characterises strict PREmonoidal (separately functorial, no interchange) rather than strict monoidal categories.

Class StrictMonoidal : Type := { strict_is_monoidal : @Monoidal C; strict_assoc_obj : ∀ X Y Z, ((X ⨂ Y) ⨂ Z)%object = (X ⨂ (Y ⨂ Z))%object; strict_unit_left_obj : ∀ X, (I ⨂ X)%object = X; strict_unit_right_obj : ∀ X, (X ⨂ I)%object = X; strict_assoc_to / strict_unit_*_to : the structural isomorphisms ARE the transported identity }   — the example's left-hand side (a strict monoidal category) exists as an in-tree class, and SymmetricMonoidal (Structure/Monoidal/Symmetric.v:103) supplies the 'symmetric' qualifier.

statement_record.book: A symmetric strict monoidal category is precisely a commutative monoid object, in the sense of Definition 5.65, in the cartesian monoidal category (Cat, ×, 1): the multiplication is the tensor functor and the unit picks out the monoidal unit object.
statement_record.intree: Monoid_of_StrictPremonoidal / StrictPremonoidal_of_Monoid : StrictPremonoidal c ≅ @MonoidObject StrictCat Funny_Monoidal c, mutually inverse on the nose — a monoid object in (StrictCat, □, 1) is a strict PREmonoidal structure.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker, and a same-name trap: the in-tree correspondence is at the FUNNY tensor □, not the cartesian ×, and its conclusion is strict PREmonoidal (a binoidal tensor with no interchange law), strictly weaker than the book's strict monoidal. The commutative/symmetric clause is absent on both sides.

gap: The book's identification — commutative monoid object in the CARTESIAN monoidal (Cat, ×, 1) = symmetric strict monoidal category — is nowhere stated. Instance/StrictCat/Premonoid.v's own header (lines 21-26) names the (Cat, ∏, 1) statement as the classical fact its funny-tensor theorem is 'the counterpart of', i.e. explicitly as not-done. I.e. a model of the presented theory determines the structure-preserving functor out of the presented PROP UNIQUELY.

Theorem Presented_factor : ∀ m n (t : Term Σ m n), fmap[PresentedInterp] (fmap[PresentedProj E] t) ≈ interp P Σ v t   — the existence half: given a valuation v of the generators satisfying the theory's equations (ESound, :139, via interpW_sound :180), PresentedInterp : PresentedCat E ⟶ P (:194) is a strict (PresentedInterp_Strict :304) symmetric (PresentedInterp_SymmetricStrict :327) monoidal functor extending v.

statement_record.book: The prop M presented by two generators μ : 2 → 1 and η : 0 → 1 subject to the three equations of Definition 5.65 deserves to be called 'the theory of monoids in monoidal categories': for any monoidal category C, the monoid objects in C correspond to strict monoidal functors M → C. This is the germ of Lawvere's algebraic theories.
statement_record.intree: Presentations by generators and equations exist generically (Record SMT { smt_sig : Signature; smt_eqs : EqSystem smt_sig }, Construction/PROP/Presentation.v:113, with the quotient PresentedCat), and the universal property of the presented PROP is proved in both halves (Presented_factor, Presented_unique): equation-respecting valuations correspond bijectively to strict symmetric monoidal functors out of the presented PROP.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker in two ways: the target is restricted to PROPs rather than an arbitrary monoidal category, and the monoid theory M itself is never instantiated, so the specific correspondence 'monoid objects in C ↔ strict monoidal functors M → C' is not stated.
